discovery: Quantum error correction and topological fault-tolerant quantum computation
motivation: Before 1995 many physicists believed decoherence made large-scale quantum computation impossible: quantum states cannot be copied, and errors are continuous. Shor and Steane independently discovered that quantum information can be protected by encoding it redundantly in entangled states, with measurements of syndromes that detect errors without disturbing the logical state. Kitaev then recast protection as a physical property of matter: toric and surface codes, where information is stored non-locally in topologically ordered systems and fault tolerance follows from local checks and a finite error threshold. These ideas founded a new field linking quantum measurement, many-body physics and topology. They now set the agenda for every experimental platform. Recent superconducting, trapped-ion and neutral-atom experiments show logical qubits whose errors fall as code size grows, below threshold, confirming the physics predicted thirty years ago. This is a conceptual discovery that has changed what physicists believe is controllable.
